emteegee · table layout study 02 · skins

The same table, in three skins.

Layout B, identical board state, identical markup — only the color tokens change. Every value is a CSS custom property on the table element, so a skin is about fifteen numbers, and adding a fourth later costs nothing.

Board

Parchment

Warm paper and aged linen. The playmat you actually own.

Warmest, most Magic. Card art sits on a ground that shares its palette, so illustrations look framed rather than pasted on. Watch the white-bordered cards in hand — they lose a little edge definition against it.

Slate

Cool neutral greys, a modern app surface with a blue accent.

Cleanest, most legible. Highest contrast for text and the crispest separation between zones. Reads like a well-built utility app — which is also the risk: it looks less like a game.

Felt

The original dark table. Art glows against it.

Best for art, hardest outdoors. Dark ground makes illustrations pop and hides the phone bezel at night, but it's the worst of the three in daylight and burns more battery on OLED than a light skin saves.
